lines: A Watch advances the Opening clock by eight hours. A normal day contains:
- Two active Watches.
- One Rest Watch for each character.
A character assigned to work during their scheduled Rest Watch gains **Rest Debt**. An attempted Rest Watch interrupted before completion also creates Rest Debt after the emergency scene ends.

Record a two-Watch countdown. The character must complete one full Rest Watch before the end of the second following Watch. At the end of that second Watch, an unpaid debt causes 1 Strain and remains owed until a full Rest Watch is completed. A character can owe only one Rest Debt at a time; missing another scheduled Rest while already indebted immediately causes 1 Strain and resets the countdown to two Watches. Completing the owed Rest clears the debt. A character cannot remove Strain until completing a safe Rest Watch.
### Short Rest
A Short Rest takes one hour. A character can benefit from no more than two Short Rests between Long Rests.
- Spend Hit Dice as permitted by class rules.
- Recover one-quarter of maximum RP, rounded down, minimum 1 for a character with an RP pool.
- An Oracle regains 1 Revelation Charge, up to maximum.
- End effects that specify a Short Rest.
### Long Rest
A Long Rest occupies one full Watch and can benefit a character only once per twenty-four hours.
- Restore HP according to the Player Rulebook.
- Restore RP and Revelation Charges.
- Recover half expended Hit Dice, rounded up.
- Remove 1 Strain in a secure camp or Haven.
- Wounds require treatment; a Long Rest alone does not remove them.

Recharge N sets a counter to N after use; reduce once at the start of the owner's regular initiative turn, whether able to act or not. Extra turns/Actions do not tick it. Outside combat tick once per 6 elapsed seconds, without double counting. Recharge 2 used on turn 1 is ready on turn 3. A positive counter can be reset/shortened at most once per ability per round. Zero counters are not legal reset targets and expend no reset use. Resets never restore RP or per-rest uses or grant an immediate activation.

An encounter is a genuine scene of uncertain opposition chosen by the Director, not a player declaration used to reset resources. No encounter gain from attacking allies, one's summons, harmless animals, helpless captives or reused corpses. Out-of-combat abilities retain all printed costs and time. Short-rest means a completed uninterrupted hour of permitted recovery; long-rest means a completed 8-hour Rest Watch. This time convention is a draft integration. Expedition pressure, supplies, safe locations and rest debt still matter. A long rest also refreshes short-rest uses; a short rest never refreshes long-rest uses. Weekly uses refresh after seven full in-world days, not repeated rests.
## Targets, concentration and control

Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's.

One concentration slot for all spells, Chants, Veinweaves, forms or zones that require concentration. Starting another ends the old before the new effect resolves, except for an explicit limited linked-effect rule. Damage prompts CON save against max(10, floor(damage/2)); incapacitation or a failed save ends concentration. The round-down convention is a deliberate pilot interpretation. Concentration does not demand a Bonus Action unless maintenance says so. For a paid 3-pulse effect, start is pulse 1; pay maintenance on each of the next 2 regular turns by turn end for pulses 2/3. Missing payment ends it at that turn's end; otherwise it ends at start of turn 4. No repeated start triggers on maintenance.

Forced movement does not provoke opportunity attacks unless explicitly stated, cannot place a creature inside solid matter, and stops at an obstacle. Grapples use the card's save/DC, can be escaped with an Action and STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against that DC, and end beyond reach. A root sets Speed 0 but does not remove Actions. Slows reduce Speed to minimum 0. Silence blocks verbal spells/audible abilities, not all thought or all class features. Charmed effects never determine a player's beliefs; use only the printed action restrictions.

No repeated hard denial without a new save and cost. For this class suite, a creature can suffer **Stunned, compelled loss of its whole Action/turn, or equivalent hard denial from a given character at most once per encounter**, across that character's class features; later such riders fail while damage and soft riders resolve normally. Record source and target. This draft guard is broader than the older Oracle-only ceiling and is an explicit balance proposal. Reaction denial, Speed reduction, penalties and Frightened do not count as whole-turn loss. Do not silently waive boss immunities, legendary defenses or anatomy.
## Damage, healing, stacking and companions

Roll once for each shared area/pulse and apply saves/defenses to each target separately; separate attacks roll separately. Halve once for a successful save and apply resistance/immunity normally. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Damage reduction from these class features uses the strongest flat reduction, then applies resistance; it cannot create negative damage or healing. Temporary HP never stack; choose the larger remaining amount. Immunity is not reduced resistance.

Repeated permanent HP recovery must consume finite RP, a per-rest use or another finite resource; a combat-generated gauge alone never enables unlimited healing. Healing cannot exceed maximum HP or erase Wounds, death consequences, debt or Corruption unless explicit. Downed is living at 0 HP; dead is different. Resurrection requires a willing soul and sufficiently intact body, obeys its time window, cannot create a duplicate and never refunds the feature on failure to meet known prerequisites. Sacrificial HP is actual unpreventable loss, cannot be redirected or paid with temporary HP, and is not damage for resource triggers. It cannot reduce the donor below 1 unless a card expressly grants a death-triggered effect.

No damage/healing copy repeats the source's costs, procs, resource generation, critical bonus dice, buffs, actions, cooldown resets or duration. Compute fractions once, capped at 100% of one stored source unless an explicit card states a separately priced higher amount. Copies still cause ordinary damage consequences, concentration checks and death. A copy cannot copy another copy. A target/source record must refer to an actual resolved event, not merely a known ability name.

Where a class card calls for a **standard companion** without a more specific profile, use: Small or Medium; AC 12+floor(PB/2); HP 2 L; walking Speed 30 ft; saves equal owner's PB; one melee or ranged attack (reach 5 ft/range 30 ft) at owner's class attack bonus, damage S d6 of the printed type. It has no independent class features, resources, loot, death triggers or extra turns. All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging attack/action total per round** unless a specifically priced feature grants more. Without a command they move and Dodge. Act immediately after owner. A standard companion lasts 1 minute, disappears at 0 HP and cannot be healed for free by dismissing/resummoning. The creation cost must be paid again. Creature-specific stat blocks override this profile only where explicitly printed.
## Ordinary spells: one explicit test configuration

Use the manifest-owned **Core Systems Known Descent V 2** class RP tables and rank costs: rank 0–9 costs 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26; Grand 32. Follow `src/data/class-spell-progression.js` for each class's rank gates and the existing spell catalog for class/school access. Having enough RP never bypasses a rank gate. Oracle has Revelation Charges, and Soldier/Warrior have no general RP spellcasting. Multiclass spell access is determined separately per class; do not add complete class pools or use total level to unlock a rank. This suite's printed pool tables are single-class; use the existing multiclass pool formula with the new constituent Core V 2 pools for mixed characters.

Four classes have no direct Core V 2 pool row. For this pilot, Crimson Agent uses the Cleric curve multiplied by 0.5; Dragoon, Monk and Thief use that curve multiplied by 0.35, rounded to nearest integer with halves upward, minimum 1. These fallback factors come from the preserved `src/data/resonance-economy.js`; they are explicitly distinguished from direct book tables. The generic Core V 2 Oracle RP row is rejected for this class suite because Oracle's protected class contract uses Revelation Charges only. Oracle never receives RP or ordinary spell access. Retune here means one recovery at the end of a completed short rest, not an unrestricted action.

For a reproducible pilot, retain the protected **Dissonance** layer with Core V 2 numeric RP costs. This combination is a new integration decision: do not also roll a second historical Burn/fizzle system on top of it. Limit=max(4, 2+PB+max(0, casting modifier)). Before a ranked cast, Dissonance at limit/limit+3/limit+6 adds 1/2/3 RP respectively; at limit+6 ordinary casters cannot cast rank 1+. At limit+3 ordinary Overcast is unavailable. A cast then adds base Dissonance 0 at rank 0, 1 at ranks 1–5, 2 at ranks 6–9. Immediate repeated casts of the same named spell add 1, 2, then 3 maximum. Another named spell resets the repeat counter but not accumulated strain. Apply the class's exact cadence reduction/vent; never infer a free RP reduction. Printed class techniques pay printed costs and cause no automatic spell Dissonance unless tagged or expressly described as spells, Echo releases or Matrix casts. For a Mage/Wizard class card tagged as a spell, use the rank printed in normalized data; its rank is fixed at acquisition and does not rise with S. Other techniques are not counterspell able unless their card says so.

Retune recovers max(0, round(max RP/4)+casting modifier), never above maximum, and clears Dissonance. A long rest restores RP and clears Dissonance. Optional 10-minute meditation once/day recovers positive casting modifier RP and reduces Dissonance by PB+positive modifier. A regular turn with no spell or magical class ability loses 1 Dissonance; an Action spent Grounding without casting loses PB instead (not both). Merely ending an encounter does not clear accumulated Dissonance. Refrain survives idle/weapon turns unless a class explicitly clears it. Lich/Necromancer may force ranked casts through Fracture; after resolution take direct unpreventable trauma equal to rank×1/2/3 at the three strained states, minimum 1, based on state before casting. This trauma cannot generate resources or trigger damage-sharing. They still pay RP and meet rank gates.
## Zero HP and recovery

A living character at zero HP is Unconscious. Core's condition already includes Incapacitated, unawareness, dropping held items and falling Prone; an adjacent hit is critical as specified there. Healing does not silently remove other independent causes of Unconscious or Prone.

While dying, make one death save at the **start of each regular initiative turn**. Roll d20 without modifiers unless a feature specifically modifies death saves. Natural 20 restores 1 HP; natural 1 adds two failures. Other results of 10 or more add one success; 9 or less add one failure. Three successes make the creature Stable; three failures make it Dead. Extra turns and Actions add no extra death saves. Stable or Dead creatures do not roll them.

Regaining positive HP or becoming Stable resets both counters. Temporary HP does not raise normal HP, end Unconscious or reset counters. Fully absorbed damage does not end Stable or add a death failure in this provisional interpretation. Independent Maiming can still cause its Wound save.

**Stabilize:** an Action and DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, or an Action using one healer's-kit use automatically, stabilizes a living dying creature at zero. It remains Unconscious and makes no death saves. Roll 1d4 once when it becomes Stable and record its absolute recovery time that many hours later. If still Stable then, it regains 1 HP. Damage reaching normal HP cancels that deadline and resumes dying with the appropriate failures. Rest and Stable recovery use the same elapsed clock, so four hours of recovery inside an eight-hour Watch do not cost twelve hours. A later rest does not separately replay the Stable healing event.

**Dead:** ordinary healing and stabilization do not restore life. Resurrection must satisfy its own willing-soul, body, time, cost and target rules. It does not automatically remove Wounds, Corruption, debts, legal death or claims upon the body. Corpses cannot supply repeated resource triggers.
## Wounds and Critical state

Each Wound imposes **-1 Constitution saves** and reduces the normal maximum number of Hit Dice recovered per long rest by one, to a minimum of zero. It does not reduce each healing die. The broader recovery rules own the normal recovery maximum and rest legality.

At three Wounds the creature is **Critically Wounded**: Speed is reduced by 10 feet, to minimum zero, and the next failed Wound save is fatal. The failure that first raises two Wounds to three is not that later failure. Core's named **Wounded** condition (paragraph 782, preserved in [the 28-condition source register](../../data/playtest/core_condition_sources.json)) explicitly summarizes these same Wounds; it does not add duplicate penalties. Its conflicting V6 predecessor is inactive in this overlay. This individual source comparison does not complete the remaining condition audit.

**New provisional healing ceiling:** while Critical, healing cannot increase HP above **max(1, maximum HP - 1)**. Maximum HP itself does not change. Gaining the third Wound does not immediately remove existing HP; a later attempted heal also cannot reduce HP. The minimum of one permits recovery when maximum HP is one and is an explicit exception to “cannot regain full HP.” Removing enough Wounds to leave Critical removes its Speed penalty and ceiling, but does not itself heal HP.
## Recovery and actual elapsed time

Preserve campaign limits: Short Rest1h, at most **two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests**; Long Rest8h, at most **one beneficial Long Rest per24 elapsed hours**. Those limits apply to serum recovery too, including non-Warrior recipients. Exact completion timestamps and IDs prevent replay. Work, travel, short rest, sleep and recreation cannot spend the same active hours twice. Unfinished/interrupted activity provides no completion benefit.

**Rest Debt order.** First complete a qualifying safe8hRestWatch and clear debt it satisfies. Then evaluate beneficial Long Rest eligibility. If eligible, apply its sourced benefits, including serum reset and one eligible expedition point when secure. Persistent food/water/source blocks still prevent expedition reduction. An additional safe RestWatch inside the24h reward cap can discharge debt but cannot restore resources, remove expedition Strain, reset the beneficial-rest clock or reset short-rest counts.

**Secure Long Rest.** Remove one eligible expedition point chosen by the patient, once the rest qualifies and no reduction block remains. This is a separate benefit from serum reset, so one actual qualifying rest may do both. Class-only serum reduction never silently removes expedition points.

**Morale Rest — NEW endpoint.** Four consecutive safe hours of voluntarily chosen recreation, without forced substance use, work, expedition travel or simultaneous sleep/ShortRest. At most one beneficial Morale Rest per24 elapsed hours. Remove one eligible expedition point. It never removes a Wound. A distinct4hMoraleRest plus an eligible8hsecureLongRest can legitimately remove two points; there is no new shared one-point cap.

**Haven care.** One full day means24 consecutive hours under qualifying Haven care/location conditions, with real care, food and water supplied under campaign rules. One active care interval per patient; interrupted care gives no completion benefit and restarting requires a fresh24h window. At completion remove all eligible ordinary expedition points; blocked/special points remain. The care window may contain separate sleep, meals and4h recreation because it is not24h of active practitioner work. Incompatible practitioner activities cannot be double-counted.
The Strain reference does not replace HP/RP/RC rest rewards or settle all supply prices, travel limits or camp security. Those systems retain their source review gates.
### FL-03 — One clock, work and rest

The campaign uses one elapsed clock. A Watch is eight hours; a day contains Morning, Afternoon and Evening Watches. Combat rounds, rests, travel, treatment and work occupy their actual time within that clock. Completing a task does not add a second Watch. Entering Haven, changing teams or starting initiative does not reset elapsed time.

A generic Watch task needs **480 active minutes** before its completion check. Feasible unfinished work can continue in another Watch, without a proportional completion reward. Exact recipes, uninterrupted training, treatment, rest and spells keep their own interruption rules. Guarding, travelling, casting, directing, interpreting, assisting or working cannot also count as incompatible rest. Passive carriage qualifies for rest only when a genuinely suitable safe berth and the actual rest requirements are satisfied.

Plan at most two active work Watches and one Rest Watch per person each day. Evening is the default Rest slot; change it prospectively before that day's first assignment. Voluntary extra noncrafting travel or guard duty can replace Rest and incur its real costs and Rest Debt. This supplies no third crafting, training, research or harvesting Watch. Emergencies still consume time and interrupt the activity underway.

Missing a scheduled Rest creates **Rest Debt**. If an emergency interrupts Rest, the debt opens after that emergency ends; otherwise it opens when the missed Rest Watch ends. Complete a qualifying safe eight-hour Rest by the end of the second following canonical Watch. If the debt remains unpaid at that deadline, gain 1 Strain once for that due event and keep owing the Rest. Missing another scheduled Rest while indebted gives 1 Strain and resets the deadline. There is no automatic additional Strain every second or every Watch merely because the same debt remains.

A safe eight-hour Rest clears the debt even when you cannot receive another Long Rest's benefits. Keep the separate limits: one beneficial Long Rest per 24 elapsed hours, two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests, the existing four-hour Morale Rest, and 24-hour Haven care. Trance reduces sleep, not the eight-hour Long-Rest requirement. Use the actual Strain and recovery chapter for what can be removed.
### FL-04 — Supply and daily support

**Supply is a basket of real goods:** 2 lb of ration-equivalent edible food, 8 pints of potable water, 1 pint of compatible lamp oil in its flask, and 0.25 lb of ordinary camp sundries. The food and water cover one Small or Medium character's daily demand; Large characters require twice those quantities. This is game accounting. Two pounds of food equal three reviewed Cooking servings; a Large food day is six servings.

Track food and water actually consumed, by recipient and lot. Ordinary partial rations credit their edible mass. A fractional magical meal never gives a fractional benefit unless its own source permits that. The same serving cannot be spent in a recipe and remain available to eat.

Oil and sundries are spent when actually used. Do not burn spare oil or throw away sound stock to satisfy an abstract daily debit. The source lamp burns one pint in six hours. One actual light may serve several people within its real illumination, with its fuel spent once. A sufficient daylight or other safe lighting plan can use no oil; extra darkness, heating or work needs its real equipment and fuel.

At each canonical 24-hour day endpoint, settle each recipient's actual food, water and necessary declared logistics support. A recipient short of any requirement gains **1 expedition Strain total for that day's shortfall**. Missing food and water does not give two Strain. Retain partial consumption credit. The unsupported day blocks Strain removal; that block can clear on a later day only with a real sufficient provisioning plan available and maintained. Crossing a gate does not erase needs: actual Haven/home support pays needs outside the expedition.

Allocate shortages before the deadline. Joining, leaving or changing size/form divides demand by actual time and diet; it never refunds goods already consumed. A diet exception removes only its stated obligation. It gives no transferable provisions, fuel or camp labor. Unsupported nonmount Tiny, Huge or Gargantuan diets require their real profiles; mounts use their separate profiles.

If an exact procedure charges **one whole Supply**, reserve and commit the entire physical basket, or a substitute that procedure actually permits. Wound treatment keeps its one-Supply cost at the start, even if treatment fails or is interrupted. Food or water genuinely consumed by its named patient or healer can credit that person's daily need once. The committed basket does not also remain in inventory or feed another person.
Applied after other modifiers. Multiple instances don't stack.
Healing
Rest (Chapter 8) or magic restores HP. Regained HP adds to current HP, up to the maximum. Dead creatures cannot regain HP until restored to life.
Dropping to 0 Hit Points
Either die instantly or fall unconscious.
When reducing a creature to 0 HP with a melee attack, you can choose to knock it out instead of killing it. It falls unconscious and is stable.
Temporary Hit Points

A buffer against damage, lost before normal HP. Cannot be healed. Do not stack (take the higher value if you gain more). Do not restore consciousness at 0 HP. Last until depleted or after a long rest, unless specified otherwise.

clericEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Wisdom is the Cleric class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Cleric levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Wisdom modifier) unless a feature explicitly substitutes another ability. Cleric technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier. Cleric technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier.

Conviction is separate from Resonance Points. Base Conviction maximum is 3, automatically becoming 5 at Cleric 9; after a long rest you begin at your current maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent Conviction, to the maximum. A completed long rest restores all Conviction. Conviction Pool raises the maximum by 2. Conviction persists between encounters; simply declaring prayer, repeating a Rite, or performing harmless actions outside a real encounter never generates Conviction.

Only explicit features generate Conviction. Sacred Chant, Sermon of Purpose, Doctrine Shield, Dark Conviction and other printed cards are valid generators. A feature cannot generate more Conviction than its text permits, and Conviction can never exceed the current maximum. Summoned creatures, friendly creatures, trivial creatures, repeated corpse manipulation and staged out-of-combat actions cannot be used to farm Conviction.

Cleric techniques use only their printed RP and Conviction costs. All RP is paid from the Cleric's Core Systems V 2 Resonance Point pool. A Cleric technique is not automatically an ordinary spell-rank cast and does not receive Overcast, spell-slot, cost-discount or spell-proc benefits unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Ordinary spells continue to use Core V 2 spellcasting rules.

Protected Dissonance interaction: once on each of your regular turns, when you spend at least 2 Conviction on a Rite or Invocation, reduce Dissonance by 1, minimum 0. The expenditure must actually occur; waived Conviction costs do not vent Dissonance. A single feature expenditure vents at most once even if it spends more than 2 Conviction. No Cleric card automatically adds Dissonance unless explicitly written.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; for this pilot, if a division requires rounding, half damage is rounded down. Sustained Cleric effects use their printed maintenance cost and Bonus Action. A control effect that persists for multiple pulses or rounds gives the target a new save at each printed pulse or at the end of each affected turn as stated.

Round recharge counters are set after resolution and decrease once at the start of the Cleric's regular initiative turn, even if the Cleric cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not create extra recharge ticks. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one recharge tick. Only a positive counter may be reset or shortened, and a named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

Healing cannot exceed maximum HP, does not remove Wounds, and does not restore a dead creature unless a card explicitly says it resurrects. No Cleric feature provides unlimited permanent HP or resource restoration outside encounters. Temporary HP does not stack with itself; use the higher value. Resurrection and corpse-based effects have explicit use limits and cannot generate repeatable corpses, XP, loot or Conviction.

Invocation Attunement is gained automatically at Cleric level 2. Choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. Only the selected path bonus becomes active. Divine Invocation uses the mode belonging to that selected path unless another feature explicitly permits a different mode. Changing Invocation Path requires a future explicit retraining rule; this draft provides none.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION FOR PLAYTEST. Cleric 1: gain the Divine Favor engine and choose 4 Base cards, at least 2 Active. Cleric 2: automatically gain Invocation Attunement and the selected Invocation Path bonus, then choose 2 additional Base cards. Cleric 3: enter Bishop and choose 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4-8 each grant one eligible Base/Arch choice, respecting each card's minimum class level. Level 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus Bishop's Mandate automatically. Level 10 choose Saint, Priest or Cultist and gain 2 Hero choices from that path. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one additional Hero choice; levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. The chosen Hero Finale is automatic at Cleric 20. ASI/feat milestones remain separate and do not consume these choices.

All acquisition gates use Cleric class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus still follows normal total-character-level rules. A multiclass character cannot use non-Cleric levels to unlock Bishop, Hero, Invocation or Finale features. Divine commands, visions and social abilities can influence actions only to the extent their exact mechanical text states; no Cleric feature can force a player character to adopt, abandon or profess a belief.

Capacity clarification: the automatic level 9 Conviction increase is a new draft completion so every Hero can pay its 5-Conviction Finale without buying Conviction Pool. Conviction Pool adds 2 at any level, yielding 5 early or 7 from 9. It never fills gained capacity immediately.

ownedCards.name: Consecrate
ownedCards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot-radius fixed zone centered at a point within 30 feet
ownedCards.effect: Consecrate. Tags: rite, zone. Create sanctified terrain. Your Consecrated Ground feature recognizes this zone. Undead creatures in the zone have -1 on attack rolls. A creature leaving the zone loses that penalty immediately. Only one Consecrate zone created by you may exist at a time; creating another ends the first.

source.originalText: Consecrate: Sanctify the ground in a 15-foot radius, creating consecrated terrain that enhances your healing abilities and weakens undead enemies.

ownedCards.name: Consecrated Ground
ownedCards.effect: Consecrated Ground. Tags: rite, healing, passive. Whenever one of your healing Rites restores HP to a living creature standing in terrain created by your Consecrate feature, that creature regains S additional HP. Apply this once per creature per Rite pulse; it is flat healing and is not itself another healing trigger.

source.originalText: Consecrated Ground: Healing allies on terrain you sanctify (via Rite) heals for +10%.

ownedCards.name: Fervent Ritualist
ownedCards.effect: Fervent Ritualist. Tags: rite, ritual, passive. When a Rite with a Ritual activation normally requires at least 10 minutes, reduce its required time by 1 minute for each full 10 minutes of its printed casting time. This never reduces a Ritual below 1 minute and does not alter Action, Bonus Action or Reaction Rites.

source.originalText: Fervent Ritualist: +10% faster channel speed on all Rites.

ownedCards.name: Healing Rite
ownedCards.effect: Healing Rite. Tags: rite, healing. One living ally regains S d8 + M HP. It cannot restore a dead creature or remove Wounds. Consecrated Ground and appropriate Invocation Path bonuses may modify this healing.

source.originalText: Healing Rite: A channeled ability that restores health to an ally, with increased effectiveness on consecrated ground.

ownedCards.name: Conviction Pool
ownedCards.effect: Conviction Pool. Tags: conviction, passive. Increase your Conviction maximum by 2. This changes only the maximum; it does not immediately restore spent Conviction when acquired during play. A long rest restores Conviction to the new maximum.

ownedCards.name: Judging Light
ownedCards.effect: Judging Light. Tags: smite, passive. When your Divine Smite damages a creature currently affected by a Cursed or Weakened condition, add S d4 radiant damage to that Smite. Roll these dice once as part of the Smite; they do not create a second hit or trigger.

source.originalText: Judging Light: Smite deals +20% bonus damage to enemies afflicted by Cursed or Weakened effects.

ownedCards.name: Invocation Attunement
ownedCards.effect: Invocation Attunement. Tags: invocation, core. At Cleric level 2 choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. You automatically gain that path's listed bonus. Divine Invocation thereafter uses that path's mode unless another feature explicitly overrides it.

source.originalText: Invocation Attunement: Choose one Invocation Path (see below); gain a permanent passive tied to it.

ownedCards.name: Radiance
ownedCards.frequency: Automatic only if Radiance was selected
ownedCards.effect: Invocation Path — Radiance. Tags: invocation, radiance, healing. Once on each of your turns when one of your Rites restores HP to at least one living creature, choose one creature healed by that Rite. It regains S additional HP and may immediately end either Frightened or Poisoned on itself.

source.originalText: Radiance: +10% healing power and heals cleanse minor conditions.
